observed_original_abi.calling_convention: __thiscall, receiver in ECX, three 4-byte callee-cleaned stack arguments
observed_original_abi.calling_convention_evidence: ECX is copied to ESI at 0x00d00a7c (`89 ce` MOV ESI,ECX) and every one of the four receiver reads is `[ESI+disp]`; the receiver is never taken from the stack. The terminator is `RET 0xc` at 0x00d00b03, 0x00d00b15, 0x00d00b2c and 0x00d00b35, so the callee pops its own three arguments and the caller pops nothing. __cdecl and __stdcall are excluded by that cleanup; a fastcall reading is not excluded by the callee's own bytes (see alternatives).
observed_original_abi.calling_convention_alternatives: __fastcall is not separable from __thiscall on this body: a fastcall would place a second argument in EDX, and this body never reads EDX except as the first forwarded stack word, which is consistent with both. The receiver framing is declared because the call sites load ECX immediately before the call and none passes a second pointer argument in a register; the callee-side evidence alone does not exclude the fastcall reading.
observed_original_abi.receiver: ECX at entry, moved to ESI at 0x00d00a7c and read at +0x10/+0x14/+0x18/+0x1c; never written
observed_original_abi.receiver_disposition: The body performs four 4-byte reads and no store through the receiver. The package models the receiver at exactly the width the body reaches (0x20 bytes, prefix 0x00..0x0f opaque) and names no member, because the derived receiver record is bounds_only with displacements [0x10,0x14,0x18,0x1c] and no owner type.

observed_original_abi.ret_form: RET 0xc, at 0x00d00b03, 0x00d00b15, 0x00d00b2c and 0x00d00b35 -- one terminator per exit
observed_original_abi.frame: SUB ESP,0x10 at 0x00d00a70 and PUSH ESI at 0x00d00a7b; ESI is popped on every exit. The 16 bytes of stack are the outgoing-argument area used by the call at 0x00d00a87 plus the two spilled clamp bounds and the spilled float, none of which outlives the call.
observed_original_abi.return_semantics: one of the five immediates 0,1,2,3,4: `XOR EAX,EAX` at 0x00d00b2f, `MOV EAX,0x1` at 0x00d00b23, `MOV EAX,0x2` at 0x00d00ade, `MOV EAX,0x3` at 0x00d00afa, `MOV EAX,0x4` at 0x00d00b0c -- one per exit, all of them integers
observed_original_abi.return_type_rationale: OBSERVED FROM THE LISTING, NOT INFERRED FROM A TYPE. Each of the five exits writes an immediate into EAX and none touches ST0 on the way out; the x87 register is consumed by `FSTP dword ptr [ESP+0x4]` at 0x00d00a8c and is dead from there on. Corroborated from the CALL SIDE: at 0x00ae2e33 the instruction after the call is `CMP EAX,0x1` feeding `SETLE CL`, and at 0x00bef633 it is `CMP EAX,0x4` feeding `SETGE CL`. Both read EAX as a small integer and neither touches the FPU, so a float return would be refuted by both sites.
observed_original_abi.float_precision: single. `FSTP dword ptr [ESP+0x4]` at 0x00d00a8c stores ST0 as a 4-byte value, and every subsequent access of that slot is MOVSS/COMISS, a single-precision form. The x87 push/pop is a transfer mechanism here, not an 80-bit computation.

observed_mechanics: the body is 58 instructions, 0x00d00a70..0x00d00b35, body span 198 bytes; the listing parse record is complete with no unparsed line at the disassembly level

instruction 0x00d00a70 SUB ESP,0x10 establishes the outgoing-argument area; 0x00d00a73/0x00d00a77/0x00d00a7e read the three incoming words at entry+0xc, entry+0x4 and entry+0x8 respectively -- note the read ORDER is third, first, second, which is why the forwarded order is by push sequence and not by read sequence
0x00d00a82..0x00d00a84 push the three words in reverse (EAX, ECX, EDX), so the callee at 0x00d00a87 sees them in argument order

the clamp is two instructions: 0x00d00ab2 MAXSS against [0x01478d5c] then 0x00d00ab8 MINSS against [0x01478d60], with the memory operand second on each. That operand position is what decides which bound an unordered value exits through.

the four band tests read [ESI+0x14] once into XMM1 at 0x00d00ac4 and keep it there; the last test at 0x00d00b18 compares against XMM1 without reloading, which is why the reconstruction loads edge14 once
all seven conditional branch targets lie inside 0x00d00a70..0x00d00b35, so the branch graph is closed inside the body; the body is a single fall-through chain, not a binary search
XMM1 is written once (0x00d00ac4) and read twice (0x00d00acf, 0x00d00b18); XMM2 is written twice (0x00d00ad4, 0x00d00af0) and never read
no instruction in the body performs a store through the receiver, through a pointer derived from it, or through any global
no indirect transfer of any kind appears in the body: no call through a register, no memory-indirect jump, no vtable-shaped load. The dispatch record agrees at zero indirect calls.

semantic_findings: 0x00d00a70 is a five-way band index. It computes one scalar, clamps it into [-10.0, +10.0], and returns which of five bands the clamped value falls in, as an integer in EAX.

The bands are NOT uniform in closure, and the asymmetry is the listing's: (-inf,f10] -> 0, (f10,f14] -> 1, (f14,f18) -> 2, [f18,f1c) -> 3, [f1c,+inf) -> 4. Band 2 is open at both ends; band 1 is closed at its top and open at its bottom. A transcription that made every band half-open or that searched an ordered array would answer differently on four of the five boundaries.

The band chain is a fall-through list in the order 2, 3, 4, 1, 0 and NOT a binary search over an ordered key. That order is observable on unsorted fixtures, and the model test pins it with three of them.

The four receiver floats are read as four independent words. Nothing in the body compares one against another, so the reconstruction does not assume they are ascending, and the model test uses deliberately unsorted fixtures to show the answers are order-independent in the way the listing requires rather than sorted.

The clamp's OPERATION ORDER is observable. MAXSS runs against the lower bound first and MINSS against the upper bound second, both with the memory operand second, so an unordered value leaves through the LOWER bound. Transposing the two operations sends the same NaN out the upper end, and the model test catches that with a fixture where -10.0f and +10.0f land in different bands.

EVERY guard in the body is a NEGATED branch (`JBE`/`JC` used as `if (taken) leave`). That is why `!JBE(a,b)` is exactly `a > b` and `!JC(a,b)` is exactly `a >= b` even on an unordered pair: COMISS sets CF=ZF=1 there, so the branch is taken, so its negation is false, which is what the arithmetic comparison also gives. The model test asserts this identity directly, so the helpers cannot drift into something the machine does not do.
The result is one of exactly five integers, for every input tried, including both infinities, NaN and a denormal. The set is closed.
The body never writes memory outside its own frame: the receiver is read four times and written never, and both globals are read-only.

The three stack words are forwarded verbatim, in the order the pushes place them, and the receiver reaches the callee in ECX. That is the whole of the forwarding behaviour and the model test pins the word values and the call count.

unresolved_questions: WHAT THE FOUR RECEIVER FLOATS ARE IS UNKNOWN, AND IT IS THE QUESTION THAT WOULD NAME THE FUNCTION. They are four compared edges on a receiver this body shares with 42 call sites, and nothing in this package's evidence writes them or shows a caller reading the answer back into them. The band partition in `semantic_findings` is therefore a description of the arithmetic, not a claim about a domain.

WHY THE RESULT IS AN INDEX RATHER THAN A VALUE IS NOT SETTLED HERE. Five ordered bands over a clamped scalar is a natural shape for a quantiser, a difficulty band or a simulation-state selector, and this evidence distinguishes none of them. The 42 call sites would: a site that stores the result to a word and later compares that word against a small constant would identify the index's consumer. This package reads two call sites and does not claim the rest.

THE CALIBRATION OF THE FOUR EDGES IS NOT OBSERVED. Nothing shows what sets 0x10..0x1c, whether they can be re-tuned at runtime, and whether they are per-receiver or shared. The clamp bounds at 0x01478d5c/0x01478d60 ARE constants in the data section, but that says nothing about the four edges.

THE UNORDERED CASES ARE TRACED, NOT MEASURED. The five band answers under an unordered receiver float are derived from COMISS's documented flag behaviour and are asserted against the reconstruction's helpers, not against the original process. A trace of the original under a NaN edge would settle them.
NO RUNTIME EVIDENCE EXISTS. Nothing in this repository has run the original process for this target, so the model test is a static model of the listing and not a differential test against the game.

focused_test.mutation_catch_detail: each mutant is REFUTED (nonzero exit from the rebuilt model test). Sixteen are refused by named runtime checks (M1..M16); eight are refused at compile time by a static_assert in the package (H1..H8), which is a refutation too, and the harness names the two mechanisms separately rather than conflating them. No mutant exited 0 and no mutant failed for an unrelated build reason.
focused_test.notable_negative_result: Degrading the comiss_jbe/comiss_jc HELPERS to the plain C++ `<=`/`<` is NOT a usable mutation for this body, and the reason is worth recording: every guard here is a NEGATED branch, and !(a <= b || unordered) is exactly `a > b`, so the helper and the operator agree on every input and no runtime case can separate them. An earlier draft of this harness did try it, and it reported as a HOLE IN THE TEST -- correctly, because it is not a hole, it is an equivalent mutation. The mutation was replaced with one that changes the GUARD instead of the helper (M13/M14), which is separable. Anyone extending this harness should not reintroduce the helper degradation and read the resulting 'not refuted' as a defect.
focused_test.counting_method: each mutant is built and run under the real gate (fresh archive per mutant: `rm -f` then `ar rc` -- `ar qc` appends and a stale object would silently win the link). Every mutant is compiled in a SELF-CONTAINED directory holding the impl .cpp, the .hpp AND the model test, because `#include "x.hpp"` resolves relative to the including file first and a test built from the package would pull in the ORIGINAL header, making every header mutation a no-op that reads as a pass.
